header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), David Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (StellarScale), Priya Rao (StellarScale), Marco Silva (StellarScale)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and StellarScale to explore reseller/integration possibilities: focus on GPU hosting capabilities, private VPC integrations, and co-benchmarks. Customer interested in joint go-to-market and technical compatibility. Agreed to next steps: share docs, plan benchmark, schedule technical deep dive.
topics: Introductions; StellarScale infra overview (fleet, AMIs, regions); Redwood product modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private); integration points (connectors, APIs, billing models); security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs); benchmarking plan and pilot scope; go-to-market partnership models
transcript:
00:00 - Ava Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, and with me is David our SE, we'll keep this casual introduce both companies goals, hopefully find some next steps.
00:08 - Liam O'Connor: Thanks Ava, yeah hi all, Liam here, head of partnerships at StellarScale. Priya and Marco from my team are on. We're excited to hear more about Redwood and how we might integrate.
00:18 - David Park: Hey Liam, Priya, Marco, good to meet you. Quick quick overview from our side - Redwood is an inference platform that can be hosted, or run as Dedicated capacity or Private in customer VPCs. We optimize latency and cost through batching, KV cache, quantization recommendations and routing policies.
00:36 - Priya Rao: Cool thanks, so from our side we run a mix of Ampere and N10 GPUs across three regions, mostly reseller-hosted racks plus our own cloud. We do a lot of ML infra for customers that need predictable throughput.
00:48 - Marco Silva: And we do marketplace integrations too, so curious about a partner flow and billing.
00:55 - Ava Chen: Great, that's right in our wheelhouse. A couple clarifying q's: are you looking to resell Redwood as a managed offering on StellarScale, or more like a technical integration where you route customer workloads to Redwood Dedicated on your infra?
01:05 - Liam O'Connor: A bit of both actually. There's interest in a white-label-ish managed inference plan for infra customers + an integration so customers can spin up instances using StellarScale images that are optimized for Redwood.
01:18 - David Park: Okay makes sense. From a tech perspective our Private deployment supports VPC peering or VPN for control plane connectivity, and on-prem/offline options. We also provide an image/AMI profile for our runtime. How are you managing customer tenant isolation today?
01:32 - Priya Rao: We use network segmentation and separate projects/accounts, and we provide iso images per customer. On isolation we need strong audit logs and KMS integration because many customers are regulated.
01:42 - Ava Chen: Awesome, that'll map to our features: we support KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys, audit logs, RBAC integrations and SSO - we can provide SOC 2 docs. We'll include the security checklist.
01:52 - Marco Silva: On perf, what kind of latency / throughput tradeoffs do you expect on GPU types? Some customers insist on <100ms token latency.
02:03 - David Park: So depends on model selection and sequence lengths, but with optimized kernels and batching we can hit low token latencies on A100/H100 class hardware for smaller context lengths; for those <100ms it's usually a smaller model or higher-provisioned Dedicated pools. We also do automatic fallback routing to cheaper variants during peak.
02:21 - Liam O'Connor: Interesting. On benchmarking, we'd like some numbers running on our fleet (Ampere + N10). Is it feasible to run Redwood runtime on our images?
02:31 - David Park: Yes; our Private deployment is designed to run on customer infra. We'll need a short compatibility checklist (drivers, CUDA/ROCm versions, kernel flags), and we typically run a small pilot - 1-2 nodes for a week.
02:45 - Priya Rao: That sounds right. Can you share the checklist now or later? we want to vet it with infra team.
02:51 - Ava Chen: We'll send the checklist as part of the integration guide. We'll also include a recommended AMI and the packaging for the runtime.
03:00 - Marco Silva: On pricing, are partner margins possible? If we resell Managed Redwood, we need some margin.
03:07 - Ava Chen: Yes, Redwood has partner programs with reseller pricing and co-selling incentives. We'll share the high-level partner program doc.
03:14 - Liam O'Connor: Security and compliance: most of our enterprise customers require SOC 2 type II and occasionally ISO. Do you have those?
03:21 - Ava Chen: We are SOC 2 compliant and will share the attestation plus the security checklist and audit log export formats (S3, SIEM connectors). Also we support customer-managed KMS.
03:30 - Priya Rao: Good. Another technical question: how do you handle prefix cache and KV caches across multi-tenant workloads? We want to avoid cross-tenant contamination.
03:40 - David Park: Good question - we partition cache per-tenant and per-model slot; we can also enable strict isolation in Dedicated/Private modes. The cache is namespaced and encrypted at rest.
03:52 - Marco Silva: Any tricky parts we should expect for our Ampere/N10 fleet?
03:56 - David Park: The main points are ensuring the right CUDA/runtime libs and some kernel options; for N10 we validate ROCm path - sometimes perf regresses if driver/kernel mismatch. We'll provide a test harness.
04:10 - Liam O'Connor: On go-to-market, we have a marketplace and channel partners. Are you open to co-marketing?
04:17 - Ava Chen: Absolutely. We do co-marketing, joint webinars, shared benchmarks for PR. We can craft a joint announcement after an initial pilot.
04:25 - Priya Rao: For the pilot, expected scope? Throughput targets?
04:29 - David Park: Typically pilot includes: deploy runtime on 1-2 nodes, run end-to-end generation workloads (chat + embeddings), collect latency/throughput/cost metrics over 48-72 hours, and test failover/fallback. We'll propose concrete SLOs based on your target models.
04:45 - Marco Silva: Ok, and who owns the billing during pilot? Usually partner provides infra and Redwood measures usage; billing TBD.
04:52 - Ava Chen: For pilot we'll treat it as a technical engagement - no immediate billing; if it's a reseller case we'll scope pricing after technical validation.
04:58 - Liam O'Connor: Competitors we see in this space are ApexCloud and Auroragpu and some self-hosted folks. Pricing and performance are key differentiators.
05:08 - David Park: Got it. We'll include a performance profile for commonly used open models and Redwood-verified numbers; that typically helps conversations.
05:16 - Priya Rao: About networking: you mentioned VPC peering and VPN - what about private control plane - do you require egress to Redwood or is it optional?
05:26 - David Park: We can run a Private control plane that is customer-managed with no egress for control plane - some customers prefer a fully air-gapped option. For the hosted control plane we naturally have egress, but data plane can be restricted. We'll document options.
05:40 - Marco Silva: Great. Any regulatory concerns for EU customers? Data residency?
05:44 - Ava Chen: We support region pinning and private deployments in EU; audit logs and data residency controls exist - we'll share the details.
05:52 - Liam O'Connor: OK cool. Quick note: would like to run a benchmark targeting these numbers: 10k tokens/sec aggregate for a 10-node pool and tail p99 latency under 200ms for chat model. Can Redwood help tune for that?
06:07 - David Park: Yes we can recommend batching and quantization profiles; we also provide autoscaling policies and burst capacity to hit peaks. We'll include recommended configs in the benchmark plan.
06:19 - Priya Rao: Can you also share expected token cost numbers? even rough ballpark helps with go-to-market.
06:25 - Ava Chen: We'll share cost profiles across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and highlight unit economics.
06:31 - Marco Silva: On legal/procurement - we'll need a partner agreement and possibly an NDA before sharing some details.
06:36 - Ava Chen: We can work with your legal team; I can send a partner NDA and a partner program one-pager.
06:42 - Liam O'Connor: Great. Any blockers on your side for the pilot?
06:45 - David Park: From infra side no, just need kernel/driver confirmation and a contact for infra to exchange AMI details.
06:52 - Priya Rao: That's Priya, I will coordinate with infra and get the spec sheet.
06:56 - Ava Chen: Perfect. We'll circle back with the integration guide, the checklist, the partner deck and propose dates for the technical deep dive next week.
07:04 - Marco Silva: Sounds good. Anything else?
07:06 - Liam O'Connor: No, that's it from us. Looking forward.
07:09 - Ava Chen: Thanks everyone, next steps recap: we'll send docs and propose technical deep dive dates; David will draft benchmark plan.
07:18 - (end)
